candidates.type_contract: Finite sequences over an exact commutative ring with 0 and 1; no floating rounding law is asserted.
candidates.law: For nonempty length n,m produce n+m-1 coefficients c[k]=Σ_i a[i]*b[k−i], treating out-of-bounds as zero; if either input empty the result is empty.
falsifiers: Cyclic convolution wraps the final coefficient into the first sample.
Cross-correlation fails reversing kernel where required by convolution.
Output shape differs from n+m-1 for nonempty inputs.
candidates.relationship: Convolution is the same coefficient law used for polynomial multiplication and FIR filtering; no FFT or DSP hardware algorithm is essential.
candidates.core_question: Is this a stable named library law (preferred), or a non-derivable distinct D10 semantic root? No Core selection without evidence.

candidates.type_contract: Rational samples and an exact positive rational period. Other numeric types require explicit separate accuracy law.
candidates.law: q[0]=p[0]; for each next i choose Δ congruent to (p[i]-p[i-1]) modulo period minimizing |Δ|; for exact half-period ties preserve the sign of the original raw difference; q[i]=q[i-1]+Δ. Empty input yields empty. This is local minimal-jump phase reconstruction, not a proof of physical phase trajectory.
falsifiers: Replacing the entire sequence with input modulo period loses accumulated revolutions.
For adjacent raw differences inside half period, altering values violates continuity law.
Half-period ties picked without stated rule make result nondeterministic.
candidates.relationship: Adjacent differences modulo period plus cumulative sum distinguish signal phase unwrapping from independent per-element MODULO; operation is still expressible in a library, not a new control primitive.
candidates.core_question: Does a composable fold+MODULO library law suffice? Select as D10 only after owner judges universal distinct identity.
